evidence: Four specialist write agents hit authorization limits while targeting repositories outside the writable workspace.
cause: Write delegation happened before validating subagent filesystem permissions.
remediation: Pilot one agent after writable-scope preflight; keep external-workspace agents read-only and apply changes from the principal agent.

evidence: Eleven wait calls exhausted configured budgets totaling approximately 1510 seconds.
cause: Workers were polled without a strict progress and takeover gate.
remediation: Wait once for at most 60 seconds, inspect progress, and take over after two no-progress observations.

evidence: Three workers were manually closed or taken over after prolonged silence.
cause: Delegated writes could not complete in their permission scope.
remediation: Delegate read-only audits outside writable roots and reserve edits for writable worktrees.

evidence: The 100000-message benchmark timed out without producing a result.
cause: Full workload ran before calibration.
remediation: Run a one-percent benchmark calibration and estimate the full timeout before the production workload.

evidence: A late default change forced another full build and an unchanged benchmark was repeated.
cause: Defaults were finalized after expensive validation and default wiring was verified with a full run.
remediation: Finalize defaults before Docker and verify argument wiring with a tiny smoke workload.

evidence: Two apply_patch calls failed under the Windows sandbox.
cause: The patch tool could not enforce the configured split writable roots.
remediation: Stage inside one writable worktree and use one supported patch path before starting broad edits.

evidence: Exact replacement, interpolation, newline, path API, parser, and staging-path mistakes required repeat work.
cause: One-off PowerShell diagnostics were not syntax-checked or tested on a single repository first.
remediation: Syntax-check generated PowerShell and pilot every inventory transformation on one repository.

evidence: Forty-five commits were authored on the excluded date; the user attributed that work to Antigravity and OpenCode.
cause: User-owned external tool window.
remediation: Preserve this event for provenance and exclude it from Codex efficiency totals.

evidence: Three apply_patch attempts failed because the Windows sandbox rejected split writable roots.
cause: The current patch tool cannot prepare the configured Windows sandbox.
remediation: Use a staged single-root edit path and do not retry the same failing tool after the first confirmed platform failure.

evidence: The first 30-repository credential scan exceeded a 10-second command timeout; the retry completed.
cause: The timeout did not account for thirty Git process startups.
remediation: Budget repository-wide Git scans from a one-repository timing sample.

evidence: Two malformed git patches, one unterminated PowerShell edit command, and one unhandled native Git stderr path required correction.
cause: Fallback editing and native-command handling were not piloted with the smallest possible change.
remediation: Pilot one minimal edit and one failing native Git call before applying a workspace-wide script.

evidence: Portfolio report exceeded 60 seconds because validation spawned repeated Git processes for each evidence type.
cause: Tracked-file inventory was queried repeatedly instead of cached once per repository.
remediation: Use one git ls-files and one porcelain-v2 status snapshot per repository, then filter in memory.

evidence: The first cached but serial Git inventory still exceeded a 30-second timeout.
cause: Repository Git snapshots remained serial.
remediation: Collect read-only Git snapshots through a bounded cross-version runspace pool.

evidence: Two invalid Measure-Command invocations and one PowerShell-7-only parallel implementation were rejected.
cause: Runtime compatibility and command shape were not checked before timing.
remediation: Read PSVersion first and use Stopwatch plus a PowerShell-5.1-compatible runspace pool.

evidence: The GitHub CLI command was attempted but gh is not installed; the REST API fallback succeeded.
cause: Tool availability was not checked before invocation.
remediation: Use Get-Command preflight and call the existing REST client when gh is unavailable.

evidence: The first local git clone failed because the restricted Windows Git shell could not create its signal pipe.
cause: Local clone required the external-repository permission path.
remediation: Use the approved local-clone path on the first attempt for external repository sources.

evidence: A large inline PowerShell edit exceeded the initial 10-second timeout before writing.
cause: Command startup and parsing cost were not included in the timeout.
remediation: Use staged files and a 30-second floor for multi-file PowerShell edits.

evidence: Repeated Docker Desktop Go validation strategies timed out: bind-mount validator, go-test stage attempts, and named-cache attempt.
cause: Multiple uncalibrated strategies were tried after one direct Go container test had already passed; Windows-to-Linux compilation dominated.
remediation: Accept the first isolated passing test as evidence, avoid repeated equivalent runs, and move cross-platform cache design to a separate kit task.

evidence: A local git fetch used an abbreviated SHA as a remote ref and failed; the full SHA succeeded.
cause: Fetch semantics were not piloted.
remediation: Always resolve and use the full commit SHA for local-clone integration.

evidence: Two aggregate waits returned no completion while worktree status already showed active progress.
cause: Progress could be observed from worktrees without waiting for final agent messages.
remediation: Inspect disjoint worktrees and wait only when integration is blocked.

evidence: Two completed specialist agents reported three apply_patch sandbox failures each.
cause: The Windows split-root patch wrapper rejected their edits.
remediation: Pilot the patch wrapper once, then use one supported staged edit path without retrying the same failure.

evidence: The embeddings/LLM-eval specialist reported three pyenv shim hangs.
cause: Interpreter resolution was not preflighted.
remediation: Resolve the absolute interpreter once before running tests.

evidence: The embeddings/LLM-eval specialist reported two malformed incremental patches.
cause: Patch changes were split before validating the first patch shape.
remediation: Validate one complete patch on a single file before incremental fan-out.

evidence: report-portfolio.ps1 rejected OutputPath because the supported parameters are MarkdownPath and JsonPath.
cause: The command was issued before reading the script parameter block.
remediation: Read the parameter block before invoking repository scripts and reuse the corrected command.

evidence: A .NET regex replacement treated dollar-anchor text in PowerShell source as replacement tokens and corrupted only the writable staging copy; syntax validation caught it before integration.
cause: Source code was passed as a regex replacement string instead of using delimiter-based substring replacement.
remediation: Use index-delimited substring replacement for source blocks and parse PowerShell immediately after every generated edit.

evidence: merge-base could not resolve a commit that existed only in another clone object database.
cause: The commit was compared before fetching the local clone into the official repository.
remediation: Fetch the source clone first, then perform ff-only merge or compare FETCH_HEAD.

evidence: The new parser rejected pre-existing Markdown-style backtick scalars and the legacy indentation-specific catalog counter.
cause: Earlier validation checked YAML by text patterns instead of parsing it.
remediation: Keep PyYAML parsing in CI and count catalog entries independent of valid sequence indentation.

evidence: validate-kit attempted to parse sync-catalog-stacks.py with the PowerShell parser.
cause: A global list insertion added a Python script to the PowerShell-only validation list.
remediation: Maintain language-specific validation lists and parse generated scripts immediately.

evidence: Local-path git clone failed in Git for Windows because sh.exe could not create a signal pipe.
cause: The cloning strategy was selected without a Windows local-transport preflight.
remediation: Prefer a short-path git worktree for local repository isolation on Windows.

evidence: Worktree checkout failed with filename-too-long errors because 111 .gradle cache files are tracked.
cause: Repository hygiene was not checked before creating a normal-length Windows worktree.
remediation: Preflight tracked build caches with git ls-files, reject them in validation, and use a short C:\tmp worktree for cleanup.

evidence: Copying templates/validate-project.ps1 into the sparse staging tree failed because the templates parent directory had not been created.
cause: The overlay staging directory was treated as a full clone during a new file-family edit.
remediation: Create destination parents for every sparse-overlay copy or use the official full clone after switching to an isolated branch.

evidence: The first parallel spawn script failed JS parsing because inline Markdown backticks terminated template literals.
cause: Prompt transport reused JavaScript template literals without escaping embedded backticks.
remediation: Use ordinary quoted strings or structured items for long agent prompts.

source_window: portfolio platform and saga parallel implementation
evidence: Four concurrent write agents reported the same account edit-reviewer limit until 2026-07-28 14:30; only portfolio-evidence-api produced substantive code and the two frontend agents produced no files.
cause: Four heavy write agents were opened simultaneously, including dependent frontends before the evidence API contract and benchmark were stable.
remediation: Cap heavy write delegation at two; preflight one writer; finish and validate the producer/API contract before starting consumers; preserve a handoff before limits approach.

evidence: The first isolated install failed because openapi-spec-validator 0.9.0 requires jsonschema >=4.26 while requirements-ci pinned 4.25.1.
cause: New validator dependencies were pinned without running a resolver compatibility preflight.
remediation: Resolve the complete pinned validation set in an isolated venv before editing CI requirements.

evidence: Two JavaScript template strings failed to parse because Markdown or PowerShell backticks appeared inside the payload.
cause: The previously recorded prompt-transport prevention rule was not applied to a generated documentation command.
remediation: Never place Markdown backticks inside JavaScript template literals; use plain payload text or structured file patches.

evidence: The first drift smoke printed success after temp writes and child-process launch had already failed; it was explicitly discarded.
cause: The diagnostic wrapper did not set fail-fast and dereferenced null results after non-terminating PowerShell errors.
remediation: Negative-test wrappers must fail fast during setup and assert both the expected message and nonzero exit code.

evidence: The validator accumulated failures but Write-Error under ErrorActionPreference Stop exposed only the first failure, hiding later drift diagnostics.
cause: The final error-reporting loop used terminating behavior unintentionally.
remediation: Emit every accumulated validation failure with ErrorAction Continue, then return exit code 1.

evidence: Working-tree manifest validation passed, but staged Git blobs for the two new contracts differed by one byte and failed SHA-256/size comparison.
cause: The source files ended with CRLF while .gitattributes normalizes them to LF in the published index.
remediation: Normalize text contracts to LF in the generator and compare manifest hashes against staged Git blobs before commit.

evidence: The first source replacement expected host newlines and did not find an LF-only anchor.
cause: The edit transformation mixed Environment.NewLine with an LF-normalized source file.
remediation: Normalize source and replacement anchors to LF before delimiter-based edits.

evidence: One dense Python one-liner had mismatched parentheses and one multiline JavaScript payload was invalid before a simpler diagnostic succeeded.
cause: The diagnostic was over-compressed instead of using a straightforward multiline program string.
remediation: Use readable multiline diagnostic source and avoid assignment expressions in shell one-liners.

evidence: Integrated apply_patch could not enforce the Windows split writable roots; direct wrapper execution returned access denied.
cause: The active Git worktree uses a .git pointer outside the writable root and the packaged apply_patch executable was not directly executable in this sandbox.
remediation: Probe apply_patch once per worktree; after this known signature, use asserted exact-context transformations and review the resulting git diff instead of retrying.

evidence: Recursive copy of the whole smoke Git repository into C:\tmp was denied and produced no target.
cause: The smoke copied unnecessary .git internals across sandbox roots.
remediation: Create smoke fixtures under the writable workspace and copy only build, source, Wrapper, Docker, and CI files.

evidence: Kafka planner smoke omitted indentless topic lists and truncated folded scalar decisions.
cause: The planner used indentation-sensitive regular expressions for structured project YAML.
remediation: Parse project.yaml once with PyYAML and consume the resulting object for manifest decisions and lists.

evidence: The same focused reviewer exceeded one 120-second and two 60-second waits before an interrupt requested an immediate verdict.
cause: The re-review scope still allowed broad commands and no explicit return deadline.
remediation: Give a four-case bounded regression checklist, continue local work, and interrupt once after the first long timeout instead of polling repeatedly.

evidence: The first positive JVM coherence smoke used an older CI fixture without setup-java and failed before exercising the intended bypass cases.
cause: The smoke reused stale generated CI instead of the current template.
remediation: Seed coherence smokes directly from the current Docker and GitHub Actions templates.

evidence: The first precommit continuity comparison read the regex match value instead of the matched line and produced an empty count.
cause: The diagnostic used Matches.Value for a label-only pattern.
remediation: Read Select-String.Line and strip non-digits; do not rerun the full validation suite for diagnostic-only failures.

evidence: python -m unittest discover -s tests -v returned ModuleNotFoundError: rag_knowledge_base
cause: Ran the documented unittest command without PYTHONPATH=src or editable installation
remediation: Use the documented PYTHONPATH=src path before rerunning tests

evidence: tools/validate-project.ps1 reached the full Docker validation and timed out after 184 seconds
cause: Pinned dependency lock introduced a Docker build path that was not yet observed to complete within the gate timeout
remediation: Run one explicit docker build with plain progress to identify dependency resolution or build progress before retrying the full gate

evidence: Initial JSON inspection concatenated schema_version as string although the field is numeric; the corrected check passed.
cause: Ad hoc diagnostic did not normalize numeric JSON fields.
remediation: Use explicit string conversion in structured diagnostics and validate against benchmark-result-v2.schema.json.

evidence: The first secret scan command used Bash || in PowerShell and failed before scanning; the corrected PowerShell command completed.
cause: Shell dialect was not checked before composing the diagnostic.
remediation: Use PowerShell-compatible exit handling in Windows workspace commands and keep shell-specific helpers in the kit.

evidence: The first manifest write stored literal backtick newline markers; Docker/Gradle still built, but YAML parsing correctly rejected the manifest.
cause: PowerShell string interpolation was assumed while composing a multi-file mutation.
remediation: Use explicit line-ending normalization plus YAML parsing immediately after generated manifest writes.

evidence: Checklist update initially stored literal backtick newline markers; the corrected normalization produced separate checklist lines.
cause: The mutation used a single-quoted PowerShell replacement with escaped line markers.
remediation: Use actual environment newlines or normalize generated text immediately before validation.

evidence: The first V2 artifact passed schema but its comparability_key rendered kumo--sdk because PowerShell parsed the colon after the variable as a scoped reference.
cause: String interpolation was not brace-delimited around the Kumo version.
remediation: Use ${kumoVersion} in colon-delimited identifiers and inspect semantic fields after schema validation.

evidence: Direct apply_patch could create one temporary file but repeatedly failed to update files in Desktop repos or a linked worktree because the Windows sandbox could not enforce split writable roots; the packaged apply_patch executable also returned access denied.
cause: The session writable root and Git worktree metadata live on different sandbox roots; retries were attempted after the first diagnostic.
remediation: After the first split-root failure, create one reviewed patch under the writable root and use git apply --check plus approved git apply, or use an isolated clean worktree with one deterministic editor path.

evidence: git worktree add failed because the first temporary directory already existed; no repository state changed.
cause: The target path was not checked before worktree creation.
remediation: Use Test-Path and a dated unique worktree directory before git worktree add.

evidence: Piping --help into Select-Object closed stdout early and produced exit 1 even though the producer was valid; rerunning without truncation returned exit 0.
cause: A short diagnostic was piped through an early-closing consumer.
remediation: Run bounded help output directly; do not truncate a process whose exit code is part of validation.

evidence: The first cherry-pick used a guessed full SHA and failed with bad object; git rev-parse in the worktree returned the authoritative SHA and the retry succeeded.
cause: The full object ID was inferred from its short prefix instead of queried.
remediation: Always run git rev-parse HEAD before cross-worktree cherry-pick.

evidence: The first parallel HEAD inspection passed @{upstream} unquoted, which PowerShell parsed as a hashtable and rejected before Git ran.
cause: A Git revision expression with PowerShell syntax significance was not quoted.
remediation: Quote Git revspecs such as '@{upstream}' in PowerShell commands.

evidence: The first metadata replacement wrote literal PowerShell newline markers; a later report insertion assumed CRLF in an LF file. Diff review caught both before commit.
cause: A single-quoted replacement string was used with escaped newline markers.
remediation: Detect the file line ending or use a structured serializer; then run git diff --check and inspect the exact diff before commit.

evidence: Expected red assertions and a lint failure rejected Promise.all before sibling outputs were surfaced.
cause: Expected nonzero commands were mixed with success-path commands in Promise.all.
remediation: Use Promise.allSettled or isolate expected failures from positive gates.

evidence: Line-ending replacement, Python 3.10 tomllib, an rg PowerShell switch, and literal wildcard copying each required one corrected retry.
cause: Host-shell and tool-version assumptions were not checked first.
remediation: Detect line endings and tool versions, keep rg arguments native, and enumerate wildcard copies explicitly.

evidence: An unfixable Ruff line stopped a chained formatter; a stash containing regenerated evidence conflicted on pop.
cause: Commands and generated artifacts were coupled across state transitions.
remediation: Run formatter and check independently; never stash evidence that will be regenerated.

evidence: Split-root apply_patch was unavailable, gh was absent from PATH, and the first verifier call omitted mandatory RepoRoot.
cause: Desktop sandbox and local command surface differed from the expected interface; verifier signature was not read first.
remediation: Use deterministic exact replacements, GitHub REST with GH_TOKEN, and inspect script parameters before invocation.

evidence: Two local Python 3.10 attempts targeted a Python 3.12 project and failed on datetime.UTC or unavailable project dependencies.
cause: The host interpreter and package environment were not checked before invoking project tests.
remediation: Read requires-python and resolve the project runtime before host-side tests; otherwise validate inside Docker.

evidence: One generated edit stored literal newline text and another interpreted a backslash sequence as a control character; diff review caught both before commit.
cause: Long document edits were composed through shell string escaping.
remediation: Use exact-context staged edits, inspect git diff immediately, and keep generated document mutations small.

evidence: CI run 30780428819 failed because Windows working-tree CRLF digests differed from Linux committed bytes.
cause: Tracked provenance inputs were hashed from mutable checkout bytes.
remediation: Hash fixture, config, and lock inputs from Git blobs at source_commit; regression-test LF/CRLF invariance.

evidence: CI run 30780766624 could not verify the benchmark source commit because checkout depth was one.
cause: The provenance gate required history that the workflow did not fetch.
remediation: Use checkout fetch-depth 0 for source-commit verification and run the gate before image build.

evidence: Two push/fetch retries were needed because the branch lacked a usable upstream/refspec.
cause: Remote branch configuration was assumed instead of inspected once.
remediation: Inspect branch, origin, and upstream together before the first push; set upstream explicitly.

evidence: The known split-root apply_patch path was retried once and the first manually assembled git patch was malformed; neither changed repository files.
cause: The existing staged-edit prevention rule was not followed on the first attempt.
remediation: Use the tested writable-stage plus exact-context transformation path immediately in this Windows workspace.

evidence: The strict audit passed, but piping formatted output through Select-Object caused an out-of-sequence formatter error and one 25.4-second rerun.
cause: Formatted PowerShell objects were truncated instead of consumed directly.
remediation: Pipe validator output to Out-Null or use its JSON artifact; never truncate Format-* output with Select-Object.

source_window: backend traffic and platform edge closure
evidence: The first #15 V2 report encoded three repetitions as workload.measured_iterations even though each repetition measured 1000 requests; semantic review caught it before publication.
cause: The shared semantic contract was not reread before implementing a project-specific V2 producer.
remediation: Read the V2 semantic contract before producer code and add a unit assertion that measured_iterations equals domain work items while execution.repeat equals independent runs.

source_window: backend traffic and platform edge closure
evidence: The first full gate completed expensive Docker work but its inline sh -lc command lost nested quoting and a replacement-character Select-String pattern matched every line.
cause: Complex POSIX syntax and Unicode probes were embedded in one PowerShell string instead of tested as versioned scripts.
remediation: Put container validation in a checked-in POSIX script and pilot each dynamic Select-String pattern against a known nonmatching string before repository scans.

source_window: backend traffic and platform edge closure
evidence: Initial Go container probes assumed gofmt was on PATH and then requested -race in Alpine without a C toolchain.
cause: Container tool PATH and CGO capability were not preflighted before selecting validation flags.
remediation: Use absolute Go tool paths in minimal images and reserve race tests for a CGO-capable image or GitHub runner.

source_window: backend traffic and platform edge closure
evidence: CI run 31770436200 passed Go gates but the non-root benchmark container could not write /results/rate-limiter-ci.json on the Linux bind mount.
cause: Windows Docker bind-mount behavior hid the Linux host-directory ownership mismatch.
remediation: Run only the benchmark writer with the Linux host UID/GID, preserve non-root service users, upload smoke evidence, and validate these workflow guards.

evidence: Two read-only MLOps audit agents returned no findings across three bounded waits and remained running after an interrupt request.
cause: The delegated audit scope was broader than the immediate critical path and lacked an early progress checkpoint.
remediation: Delegate one repository with a 60-second evidence checkpoint; take over after two empty waits.

evidence: The first multi-stage runtime image installed the wheel but omitted source and test paths required by repository lint and architecture gates.
cause: Runtime execution needs and inspection-gate needs were treated as identical image contents.
remediation: Retain the offline installed wheel and copy only source, tests, and validation tools needed by container gates.

evidence: A 1000-row smoke execution initially emitted measured_iterations=100000 and the canonical rows comparability key.
cause: The V2 producer loaded canonical workload configuration after the command overrode rows.
remediation: Derive an effective configuration from actual command arguments, assert raw work-item counts, and regression-test overrides.

evidence: CI run 31773121400 could not verify the canonical V2 source commit because checkout history was shallow.
cause: The workflow verified historical provenance without fetching source history.
remediation: Use fetch-depth 0 in publication workflows and enforce that guard in repository validation.

evidence: CI run 31773243580 passed contract, Docker, lint, and tests but the benchmark clean-tree gate found generated editable-install metadata.
cause: pip install -e generated src package metadata that was not excluded from Git status.
remediation: Ignore generated egg-info, coverage, and cache artifacts while preserving the benchmark clean-tree gate.

evidence: Two telemetry attempts used phase and outcome values outside the recorder ValidateSet and wrote no records.
cause: Recorder enum values were assumed instead of read before invocation.
remediation: Read parameter ValidateSet values once before recording a batch of execution events.

evidence: Three canonical runs passed, but host Python 3.10 could not import datetime.UTC while aggregating evidence.
cause: Aggregation used the host interpreter even though Python 3.12 was the pinned benchmark runtime.
remediation: Run evidence aggregation inside the pinned image and keep host PowerShell limited to orchestration.

evidence: The first multi-stage image installed the wheel but omitted source and aggregation files required by repository gates.
cause: Runtime-only image contents were selected before enumerating validation and publication entrypoints.
remediation: List image entrypoints before the first build and copy only the source, tests, contracts, and evidence tools each gate executes.

evidence: The resumed benchmark wait returned timeout after the desktop task had been paused; all three run files were already complete and valid.
cause: Wall-clock timeout included an inactive desktop-task pause rather than active agent execution.
remediation: On resume, inspect durable artifacts first and mark inactive pause windows excluded instead of rerunning completed benchmarks.

evidence: CI run 32445884343 passed Python quality but the non-root Collector could not write a checkout bind mount on Ubuntu.
cause: The evidence path was validated on Windows Docker Desktop, whose bind-mount permission behavior did not reproduce Linux UID ownership.
remediation: Initialize named evidence and result volumes from directories owned by the runtime UID, then copy artifacts explicitly after the container exits.

evidence: CI run 32446166939 passed the live benchmark but could not read the historical source commit referenced by publication evidence.
cause: The publication job used the checkout default depth even though this defect and remediation were already recorded for data-quality-checks.
remediation: Make fetch-depth 0 a reusable publication-workflow guard whenever evidence references any commit other than the checked-out head.
